--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AI-1] Unbounded multi-LLM pipeline per request
File: actions/context.ts (L860-L1060)
Evidence: generateDocsWithStreaming (called by src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts) runs a sequence of full LLM calls: numberOfPhases -> generatePRDStreaming -> generatePlanStreaming -> generateProjectStructureStreaming -> generateUIUXStreaming -> loop calling generateNthPhaseStreaming for each phase, awaiting each call. Each incoming /generate-docs-stream POST triggers all those LLM calls every time with no result caching.  
Impact: Cost multiplies with numberOfPhases and users (per-request cost = ~6 + N LLM calls), producing unbounded linear growth per user request that can quickly exhaust budget and quotas.  
Fix: Cache results by a deterministic hash of (messages, architectureData) and return cached artifacts; enforce max phases per request and early-return when cached.

[AI-2] Large repeated prompt payloads risk token overflow
File: actions/context.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: Multiple generators format prompts by JSON.stringify(architectureData)/prd/plan and pass full conversation_history into ChatOpenAI without token counting, truncation, or summarization (e.g., prompt.format({ architecture_data: JSON.stringify(architectureData), ... })).  
Impact: High probability of exceeding model context windows under realistic architectureData sizes or long histories, causing silent failures or truncated responses; cost also spikes because huge prompts inflate tokens (unbounded per request).  
Fix: Add a token-counting step (tiktoken), truncate or summarize architectureData/chat history before sending, and move large documents into embeddings/retriever or reference stored summaries.

[AI-3] No rate limiting or per-user budget caps on AI route
File: src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: The SSE POST handler immediately calls generateDocsWithStreaming for any request and returns a streaming Response; there is no throttling, per-user quota

--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AI-1] Unbounded multi-LLM pipeline per request
File: actions/context.ts (L860-L1060)
Evidence: generateDocsWithStreaming (called by src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts) runs a sequence of full LLM calls: numberOfPhases -> generatePRDStreaming -> generatePlanStreaming -> generateProjectStructureStreaming -> generateUIUXStreaming -> loop calling generateNthPhaseStreaming for each phase, awaiting each call. Each incoming /generate-docs-stream POST triggers all those LLM calls every time with no result caching.  
Impact: Cost multiplies with numberOfPhases and users (per-request cost = ~6 + N LLM calls), producing unbounded linear growth per user request that can quickly exhaust budget and quotas.  
Fix: Cache results by a deterministic hash of (messages, architectureData) and return cached artifacts; enforce max phases per request and early-return when cached.

[AI-2] Large repeated prompt payloads risk token overflow
File: actions/context.ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: Multiple generators format prompts by JSON.stringify(architectureData)/prd/plan and pass full conversation_history into ChatOpenAI without token counting, truncation, or summarization (e.g., prompt.format({ architecture_data: JSON.stringify(architectureData), ... })).  
Impact: High probability of exceeding model context windows under realistic architectureData sizes or long histories, causing silent failures or truncated responses; cost also spikes because huge prompts inflate tokens (unbounded per request).  
Fix: Add a token-counting step (tiktoken), truncate or summarize architectureData/chat history before sending, and move large documents into embeddings/retriever or reference stored summaries.

[AI-3] No rate limiting or per-user budget caps on AI route
File: src/app/api/generate-docs-stream/route.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: The SSE POST handler immediately calls generateDocsWithStreaming for any request and returns a streaming Response; there is no throttling, per-user quota check, or request costing/billing guard in the handler.  
Impact: A traffic spike or abusive client can trigger many heavy multi-call LLM jobs and exhaust API quota (linear-to-unbounded growth across concurrent users).  
Fix: Enforce per-user and per-IP rate limits, require/verify user credits or quota before starting heavy generation, and reject or queue excessive requests.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AI-4] Sequential per-phase LLM calls create latency and lost batching opportunities
File: actions/context.ts (L900-L1060)
Evidence: generateDocsWithStreaming awaits generateNthPhaseStreaming inside a for-loop, executing N full streaming LLM calls sequentially instead of batching or controlled parallelism.  
Impact: High end-to-end latency for multi-phase jobs; throughput could be improved and latency reduced by batching safe parallel calls or limiting concurrency (cost remains similar but UX degrades).  
Fix: Parallelize independent phase generation with concurrency limits or batch generation where prompts can be combined; add a job queue and background workers to smooth spikes.

--- INFO ---

[AI-5] Token usage handler exists but not integrated
File: common/TokenUsageHandler.ts (L1-L80)
Evidence: Repo includes TokenUsageCallbackHandler to aggregate token counts from LangChain outputs, but the large context.ts LLM calls do not wire this callback into ChatOpenAI or chains.  
Usefulness: Implementing and logging this handler on LLM calls would enable real-time cost visibility and help enforce budget caps.
